evals.name: atlas-fullstack-erp
evals.prompt: work on WWPeps. explore the entire codebase. build graph for the entire pipelines it have, all the work flows, all exact functions listed out
evals.expected_output: A published artifact mapping every pipeline in the WWPeps round workflow, with SVG mechanism diagrams, exhaustive function and endpoint indexes, and traps found in the source.
assertions: Produced a self-contained HTML document, not a markdown or plain-text file
Contains at least 2 inline <svg> diagrams, each with both a viewBox and an aria-label
validate.py reports no structural problems (tag balance, TOC/section match, tables wrapped)
contrast.py reports every SVG colour legible on BOTH theme grounds
Theme tokens are defined in all three places: bare :root, prefers-color-scheme dark guarded by :not([data-theme=light]), and [data-theme=dark]
terminal-report.md names at least one specific finding citing a real file or function, rather than a generic summary of the document

verify_claims.py surfaces no unexplained fabricated identifiers: anything it flags is either a proposed new thing, a file on the server rather than in the repo, or a checker artifact — screening tool, reviewed by hand, not a raw pass/fail threshold
Includes an exhaustive function index whose row count is within 20% of inventory.py ground truth
Includes a route/endpoint or module-surface index grounded in the real repo
Explains at least one mechanism (a gate, a state transition, an invariant) rather than only listing inventory

evals.name: changespec-loose-notes
evals.prompt: these are the latest notes from the shuda ops meeting. expand on this, organize it, and tell me precisely how to wire this into the current system. i want to know everything that changes.
evals.expected_output: A published artifact decoding each note against the real ShudaLogistics code: requirement register, schema changes, breaking changes, open questions, phased build order.
assertions: Produced a self-contained HTML document, not a markdown or plain-text file
Contains at least 2 inline <svg> diagrams, each with both a viewBox and an aria-label
validate.py reports no structural problems (tag balance, TOC/section match, tables wrapped)
contrast.py reports every SVG colour legible on BOTH theme grounds
Theme tokens are defined in all three places: bare :root, prefers-color-scheme dark guarded by :not([data-theme=light]), and [data-theme=dark]
terminal-report.md names at least one specific finding citing a real file or function, rather than a generic summary of the document
All 10 input notes appear as distinct decoded requirements, including the Chinese-language note about zone capacity limits
Contains an explicit 'what breaks' analysis that references existing code paths in the repo
Contains at least 5 open questions the client needs to answer
Contains a phased build order with independently deployable phases
Every cited file path either exists in the repo, is clearly described as a new file to create, or is an infrastructure file the document says lives on the server
Identifies at least one collision or contradiction between the notes and what the code already does
